SELECT i.sku, i.stock_count, i.reorder_point, i.location, i.last_restocked_at, 
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory_items WHERE sku = i.sku AND quantity_on_hand > 0) AS actual_count, 
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory_items WHERE sku = i.sku AND quantity_on_hand = 0) AS expected_count
FROM inventory i;

This is likely due to a combination of factors, including poor demand forecasting, inadequate inventory management, and potential supply chain disruptions. The high reorder points for some products, such as OIL (63) and SHIRT (30), suggest that these items may have been over-ordered in the past, contributing to the current stockout.
detections.recommendation: Immediately implement a just-in-time (JIT) inventory replenishment strategy to quickly restock depleted products. Conduct a thorough review of demand forecasting models and adjust them to better reflect actual demand patterns, and consider implementing a vendor-managed inventory (VMI) system to improve supply chain visibility and control.
